Examples

These examples follow main for release target v0.4.3. For an installed v0.4.2 release, use the examples at that tag; see CHANGELOG.md for version-specific behavior changes.

For authenticated producer/consumer credentials, Go SDK key management, console and MCP workflows, see Access keys (v0.3.1 and later).

Copy-runnable examples for the four ways to use mqlite: embedded in-process, the transactional outbox (the killer feature), a remote client with a hands-off consumer, and raw curl. Full API: api-reference.md.

1. Embedded (in-process, no broker)

One SQLite file, no network, no second process.

package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"time"

	"github.com/mqlitehq/mqlite"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mq, err := mqlite.OpenEmbedded(ctx, "file:./mq.db")
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer mq.Close()

	if err := mq.CreateQueue(ctx, "orders", mqlite.QueueConfig{
		LockDuration:     30 * time.Second,
		MaxDeliveryCount: 5,
	}); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}

	// produce
	if _, err := mq.SendOne(ctx, "orders", mqlite.OutMessage{Body: []byte(`{"id":42}`)}); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}

	// consume (Peek-Lock): receive, do work, then Complete
	msgs, err := mq.Receive(ctx, "orders", mqlite.RecvOpts{Max: 10, Wait: 5 * time.Second})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, m := range msgs {
		fmt.Printf("got: %s\n", m.Body)
		// Alternatives: Abandon retries below max and sends a failed final attempt
		// to the DLQ; Reject sends directly to the DLQ.
		if err := m.Complete(ctx); err != nil {
			log.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
}

2. Transactional outbox (the killer feature)

Commit a business write and the enqueue in one SQLite transaction — the message is enqueued if and only if the business change commits. No dual-write race, no separate outbox poller. Embedded-only (same DB).

Run this demonstration once in a fresh directory: it creates app.db and inserts the fixed sample order ID 42. A real application supplies its own order identity and retry/reconciliation policy.

package main

import (
	"context"
	"log"

	"github.com/mqlitehq/mqlite"
	"github.com/mqlitehq/mqlite/engine" // EngineTx + engine.OutMessage are used inside Tx
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	mq, err := mqlite.OpenEmbedded(ctx, "file:./app.db")
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer mq.Close()
	if err := mq.CreateQueue(ctx, "order-events", mqlite.QueueConfig{}); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}

	// Initialize this example's application-owned table. Real applications can
	// create their business schema through their normal migration process.
	if err := mq.Tx(ctx, func(tx *engine.EngineTx) error {
		_, err := tx.SQL().ExecContext(tx.Context(),
			`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS orders (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, total INTEGER NOT NULL)`)
		return err
	}); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}

	// Your app tables live in the same DB. Tx gives you that transaction.
	err = mq.Tx(ctx, func(tx *engine.EngineTx) error {
		// 1) the business write, on the SAME transaction. Use tx.Context(), NOT the ctx you
		//    passed to Tx: on a local store, cancelling a statement mid-transaction leaks the
		//    SQLite connection and wedges the database.
		if _, err := tx.SQL().ExecContext(tx.Context(),
			`INSERT INTO orders(id, total) VALUES(?, ?)`, 42, 1999); err != nil {
			return err // rollback: nothing enqueued
		}
		// 2) enqueue in the same tx — commits atomically with the write above:
		_, err := tx.SendOne("order-events", engine.OutMessage{Body: []byte(`{"order":42}`)})
		return err
	})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	// Either both happened, or neither did.
}

For local transactions, tx.Context() is deliberately not cancellable. Raw tx.SQL() statements can still execute after the original caller cancels: check ctx.Err() between business statements and return promptly. Mqlite-owned statements such as tx.SendOne have their own checks. Cancellation observed before commit rolls back all the transaction's writes, even if the callback returns nil. Use raw SQL only with caller-owned tables; directly modifying mqlite's internal tables is unsupported. See the cancellation contract.

3. Remote client + hands-off consumer

Talk to a running broker over HTTP. The Receiver runs a managed consume loop: return nil → Complete, return an error → Abandon (redelivery below the maximum; the failed final attempt goes to the DLQ), with auto lock-renewal and configurable concurrency.

The core calls in this example also work with MQLite Remote Client for Go, the standard-library-only, remote-only companion module. Install github.com/mqlitehq/mqlite-go@v0.1.2 and change the import to mqlite "github.com/mqlitehq/mqlite-go". Its source floor is Go 1.13. Use the main module shown below when the same application also needs embedded mode, Observe, or managed access-key administration.

package main

import (
	"context"
	"log"

	"github.com/mqlitehq/mqlite"
)

func main() {
	ctx := context.Background()
	cli, err := mqlite.Open(ctx, "https://your-mqlite.fly.dev", mqlite.WithToken("mqk_prod_xxx"))
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer cli.Close()

	// produce
	if _, err := cli.SendOne(ctx, "orders", mqlite.OutMessage{Body: []byte("hi")}); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}

	// nil -> Complete; error -> Abandon (retry below max; DLQ at max).
	// Auto-renew the lock; run up to 4 handlers concurrently.
	err = cli.Receiver("orders", mqlite.WithAutoRenew(), mqlite.WithConcurrency(4)).
		Run(ctx, func(ctx context.Context, m *mqlite.Message) error {
			return process(ctx, m.Body) // honor cancellation; MUST stay idempotent
		})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}

func process(ctx context.Context, body []byte) error {
	select {
	case <-ctx.Done():
		return ctx.Err()
	default:
		log.Printf("got: %s", body)
		return nil
	}
}

WithAutoRenew keeps the current delivery attempt alive; it does not spend another delivery_count. Each successful renewal keeps the later of the existing lease deadline and the broker's fresh now + lock_duration candidate (capped at a fixed subscription expiry), rather than adding a duration to the old deadline. It must arrive before the current lease expires and it cannot extend message TTL or a fixed subscription lifetime. The Receiver retries transient renewal failures while the known lease still leaves time. It starts earlier when the previous response measured a material round trip, leaving transport headroom before the conservative local deadline. If an exact confirmed lease is shorter than the minimum safe cadence, or renewal is rejected or cannot be confirmed before that deadline, it cancels the individual handler context and skips Complete/Abandon for that stale delivery. The handler must honor ctx.Done() and remain idempotent: another consumer may receive the message after the lease is lost. Exact Complete and Abandon requests share a five-second total settlement budget, including the first request and replays after a lost acknowledgement; the broker's settlement receipt makes that replay safe. If a broker or intermediary returns HTTP 499, it is retried while the Receiver's own context remains live, using the same Receive attempt ID. If a proxy removes both broker-time headers, WithErrorHandler receives one degraded-clock diagnostic.

4. Topic subscription lifecycle

Use one stable subscription for high-rate request/reply traffic and route replies inside the consumer by a globally unique correlation_id. A subscription per request adds metadata and cleanup work to the single writer.

For a remote broker, open the two clients below with separate listen and manage keys. Subscription creation/filter updates are application operations, while broker-wide inventory and both deletion modes remain administrative.

listener, err := mqlite.Open(ctx, endpoint, mqlite.WithToken(listenerToken))
if err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}
defer listener.Close()
manager, err := mqlite.Open(ctx, endpoint, mqlite.WithToken(managerToken))
if err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}
defer manager.Close()

if err := listener.Subscribe(ctx, "replies", "checkout-instance-7", nil); err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}

// For a genuinely temporary listener, TTL is the cleanup path. It is fixed at
// first creation; a manager may explicitly retire the subscription earlier.
if err := listener.SubscribeWithOptions(ctx, "replies", "checkout-request-01J...", nil,
	mqlite.SubscribeOptions{TTL: 15 * time.Minute}); err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}

page, err := manager.ListSubscriptionsWithOptions(ctx, mqlite.ListSubscriptionsOptions{
	Topic: "replies",
	Limit: 100,
})
if err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}
log.Printf("subscriptions=%d first-page=%d", page.Total, len(page.Subscriptions))

// Empty-only by default. Drain and settle retained replies before retirement.
if err := manager.DeleteSubscription(ctx, "replies", "checkout-instance-7"); err != nil {
	log.Fatal(err)
}

For intentional abandonment, call DeleteSubscriptionWithOptions with mqlite.DeleteSubscriptionOpts{Force: true}. Force can discard locked work whose external side effects already happened. The operation may finish as deleting; keep ownership of the globally unique, one-use name and reconcile it through a paged list with IncludeDeleting: true. Do not replay a destructive request after an unknown transport outcome. At a fixed deadline the temporary subscription is unavailable immediately and expiry preauthorizes force cleanup. Use globally unique one-use names; after physical cleanup, same-name creation begins a new lifetime and the name-only API cannot distinguish it from a delayed old retry.

5. curl (raw HTTP)

Any language can drive the broker — it's one POST per operation. (body is base64.)

HOST=https://your-mqlite.fly.dev
T=mqk_prod_xxx

curl $HOST/                                   # discovery (open, no auth)

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"name":"orders","config":{}}' \
  $HOST/mqlite.v1.AdminService/CreateQueue

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data "{\"queue\":\"orders\",\"messages\":[{\"body\":\"$(printf hi | base64)\"}]}" \
  $HOST/mqlite.v1.QueueService/Send

# receive -> returns seq_number + lock_token
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"queue":"orders","max_messages":1,"wait_time_ms":5000}' \
  $HOST/mqlite.v1.QueueService/Receive

# complete with the lock_token from the receive
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $T" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"queue":"orders","seq_number":1,"lock_token":"<token>"}' \
  $HOST/mqlite.v1.QueueService/Complete
